_about: PREVIEW-01 AC-19 section 7 (T14). Rollback per platform family. Every entry names the Cisco page it comes from; every command is copied character for character from that page (checked 2026-11-22 by @cto, reviewed by @ciso). An entry without commands is the fallback: 'Rollback: follow Cisco's upgrade guide for <family>' plus the link. Never add a command that is not printed on the cited page. 2026-11-27 (@cto, @ciso P1/P4): the nx-os incompatibility step is copied from the cited page, Downgrade step 3 (Cisco's example image nxos.9.2.1.bin); the install all command is the same for upgrade and downgrade. ios-xe-install says the cited guide covers Catalyst 9000.

families.label: IOS XE, install mode
families.source_title: Upgrade Guide for Catalyst 9000 Switches (Cisco), sections Install Abort and Roll Back Install Mode

steps.text: Cisco's guide cited here covers Catalyst 9000 switches; for other IOS XE platforms, see their own upgrade guide. Before install commit: abort the upgrade. The device reloads into the previous version.
After install commit: list the rollback points and roll back to one (1 is the id in Cisco's example; use the id from your list).

families.label: IOS (classic)
families.source_title: Upgrading the Cisco IOS Software (Cisco 3900, 2900 and 1900 Series Software Configuration Guide)

families.label: NX-OS (Nexus 9000)
families.source_title: Cisco Nexus 9000 Series NX-OS Software Upgrade and Downgrade Guide, Release 10.5(x), Downgrade to an earlier software release

steps.text: Before the downgrade, run Cisco's incompatibility check for the older image (software, then hardware) and disable any features Cisco reports as incompatible. nxos.9.2.1.bin is the image in Cisco's example; use the file name of your previous image.
commands: show install all impact nxos bootflash:nxos.9.2.1.bin

steps.text: Rollback on NX-OS is a downgrade, and it is disruptive. Cisco: the only supported method is the install all command. Save the configuration first, then install the previous image and watch the status.

Removes a patch from this node only, and the node reboots. In a deployment, roll back from the PAN first (GUI: Administration > System > Maintenance > Patch Management, Rollback). Patches are cumulative: remove the newest one first. A release upgrade (not a patch) follows Cisco's upgrade guide.
commands: patch remove <application name> <patch file number to be removed>

steps.text: Cisco's rollback plan for vSmart and vBond: activate the older image on the affected device.
